--- title: "ICP - NOC Nanopore Tree of Life Metabarcoding - analysis report" author: "Nathan" output-file: index.html format: html: toc: true toc-depth: 3 theme: cosmo code-fold: true code-block-bg: true editor: source execute: echo: TRUE warning: false message: false --- # 🧭 Introduction This project evaluates the use of Oxford Nanopore Technologies (ONT) sequencing combined with a Tree of Life metabarcoding approach for broad-scale marine biodiversity assessment. Environmental DNA (eDNA) samples were collected using the **RoCSI autonomous sampling system** and subsequently analysed using the **portable MinION sequencing platform**, providing a workflow that combines autonomous marine sampling with rapid, portable molecular analysis.

The NOC’s Robotic Cartridge Sampling Instrument (RoCSI).

The Oxford Nanopore MinION sequencing device.

The study uses 33 seawater samples collected during the **BIO-Carbon II** cruise aboard the *RRS James Cook*, along a transect extending from northern Scotland to Cardiff and covering much of the west coast of Great Britain. The transect spans contrasting marine environments and substantial gradients in environmental conditions, including temperature, salinity and chlorophyll concentration, providing a valuable test bed for assessing the ability of ONT metabarcoding to characterise biodiversity across different marine habitats. ![](figures/Map.png){fig-cap="Map of UK showing the chlorophyll concentrations and the location of the samples" width="100%" fig-align="center" } By integrating portable nanopore sequencing with autonomous eDNA sampling, the project also contributes to the development of faster and more scalable approaches to marine biodiversity monitoring. Ultimately, such workflows could support the transition from conventional retrospective eDNA analysis towards near-real-time biodiversity observations at sea. ## Metadata plots Before looking into the metabarcoding data, let's have a quick look at the metadata. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} library(dplyr) library(readxl) library(tidyverse) library(stringr) library(tibble) library(Biostrings) library(ggOceanMaps) library(ggspatial) # # Metadata → rownames = barcodeXX # meta <- read_xlsx("data/Metadata_JC269_UKWC.xlsx") # # meta <- meta %>% # mutate( # Lon = as.numeric(Lon), # Lat = as.numeric(Lat) # ) ``` ::: # 🧬 Sequencing and bioinformatics overview Six metabarcoding markers were used to characterise complementary components of marine eDNA biodiversity. For each marker, **33 environmental samples and two negative controls** (extraction and PCR controls) were analysed, representing **210 sequencing libraries**. - **16S rRNA V4:** Bacteria and archaea - **18S rRNA V4:** Eukaryotes, including protists and phytoplankton - **COI:** Metazoans - **12S rRNA (MiFish):** Fish - **ITS:** Primarily fungi - **rbcL:** Photosynthetic organisms, particularly diatoms Amplicons were sequenced at the **Centre for Genomic Research (CGR), University of Liverpool**, using Illumina MiSeq i100 paired-end sequencing (2 × 300 bp). ## Metabarcoding markers and primers ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} library(knitr) library(kableExtra) primers <- tibble::tribble( ~Marker, ~`Fragment (bp)`, ~Primer, ~`Sequence (5′–3′)`, ~Reference, "16S V4", "~252", "515F_mod_CGR", "GTGYCAGCMGCCGCGGTAA", "Parada et al.", "16S V4", "~252", "806R_mod_CGR", "GGACTACNVGGGTWTCTAAT", "Apprill et al.", "18S V4", "~400", "TAReuk454FWD1_CGR", "CCAGCASCYGCGGTAATTCC", "Stoeck et al., 2010", "18S V4", "~400", "TAReukREV3_CGR", "ACTTTCGTTCTTGATYRA", "Stoeck et al., 2010", "COI", "~313", "mlCOIintF_CGR", "GGWACWGGWTGAACWGTWTAYCCYCC", "Leray, 2013", "COI", "~313", "jgHCO2198_CGR", "TAIACYTCIGGRTGICCRAARAAYCA", "Folmer et al., 1994", "MiFish (12S)", "~170", "MiFish-U-F_CGR", "GTCGGTAAAACTCGTGCCAGC", "Miya et al., 2015", "MiFish (12S)", "~170", "MiFish-U-R_mod_CGR", "CATAGTGGGGTATCTAATCCCAGTTTGT", "Stoeckle et al., 2022", "ITS2", "~250", "ITS3", "GCATCGATGAAGAACGCAGC", "White et al., 1990", "ITS2", "~250", "ITS4", "TCCTCCGCTTATTGATATGC", "White et al., 1990", "rbcL", "~312", "708F-DEG", "AGGTGAAGYWAAAGGTTCWTAYTTAAA", "Vasselon et al., 2017", "rbcL", "~312", "R3-DEG", "CCTTCTAATTTACCWACWACWG", "Vasselon et al., 2017" ) primers |> kbl( format = "html", escape = TRUE, align = c("l", "c", "l", "l", "l") ) |> kable_styling( bootstrap_options = c("striped", "condensed"), full_width = FALSE, position = "center" ) |> column_spec(1, width = "115px", bold = TRUE) |> column_spec(2, width = "95px") |> column_spec(3, width = "195px") |> column_spec(4, width = "285px", extra_css = "font-family: monospace; font-size: 0.9em;") |> column_spec(5, width = "150px") |> collapse_rows( columns = 1:2, valign = "middle", row_group_label_position = "stack" ) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} `````{=html}

````` ::: ::: **Library preparation:** CGR overhang sequences were added to the 5′ ends of the forward (`ACACTCTTTCCCTACACGACGCTCTTCCGATCT`) and reverse (`GTGACTGGAGTTCAGACGTGTGCTCTTCCGATCT`) primers. These overhangs are excluded from the sequences in the table. ## Bioinformatics processing parameters Primer trimming was performed with **Cutadapt v5.2**, followed by ASV inference and taxonomic assignment using **DADA2**. For all markers, Cutadapt used an **error rate of 0.1**, minimum primer **overlap of 15 bp**, **no indels** and `--discard-untrimmed`. Both forward and reverse primer matches were required. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} params <- tribble( ~Marker, ~`Truncation R1/R2 (bp)`, ~`Taxonomic reference`, "16S", "250 / 250", "SILVA 138.2", "18S", "270 / 255", "PR2 5.1.0", "COI", "260 / 260", "MIDORI2 GB273", "MiFish", "None", "MitoFish (Jul 2026)", "ITS", "270 / 270", "UNITE (Feb 2025)", "rbcL", "250 / 250", "Diat.barcode 16.3" ) params |> kbl( format = "html", align = c("l", "c", "l"), escape = TRUE ) |> kable_styling( bootstrap_options = c("striped", "condensed"), full_width = FALSE, position = "center" ) |> column_spec(1, bold = TRUE, width = "90px") |> column_spec(2, width = "190px") |> column_spec(3, width = "190px") ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} `````{=html}
Marker Truncation R1/R2 (bp) Taxonomic reference

COI 260 / 260 MIDORI2 GB273
MiFish None MitoFish (Jul 2026)
ITS 270 / 270 UNITE (Feb 2025)
rbcL 250 / 250 Diat.barcode 16.3
````` ::: ::: **DADA2 settings shared across markers:** - **Filtering:** `maxEE = c(2,3)`, `maxN = 0`, `minLen = 200`, `rm.phix = TRUE`. - **Denoising:** Independent forward/reverse error models, with `pool = "pseudo"`. - **Paired-end merging:** `minOverlap = 90`, `trimOverhang = TRUE`. - **Chimera removal:** `method = "consensus"`, `allowOneOff = FALSE`. - **Taxonomy:** `assignTaxonomy()` using marker-specific reference databases; 16S species-level assignment additionally used `addSpecies()`. Truncation lengths are expressed as R1/R2 in base pairs. "None" indicates no fixed-length truncation. Other unspecified settings used DADA2 defaults. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} data_dir <- "data/Illumina" markers <- c("16S", "18S", "COI", "MiFish", "ITS", "rbcL") for (m in markers) { track <- readRDS(file.path(data_dir, paste0(m, "_read-count-tracking.rds"))) seqtab <- readRDS(file.path(data_dir, paste0(m, "_seqtab_nochim.rds"))) taxa <- readRDS(file.path(data_dir, paste0(m, "_taxa.rds"))) assign(paste0("track_", m), track) assign(paste0("seqtab_", m), seqtab) assign(paste0("taxa_", m), taxa) } ``` ::: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} qc_samples <- map_dfr(markers, function(m) { track <- get(paste0("track_", m)) seqtab <- get(paste0("seqtab_", m)) # Check sample matching stopifnot(setequal(rownames(track), rownames(seqtab))) # Match tracking rows to ASV table rows track <- track[rownames(seqtab), , drop = FALSE] tibble( marker = m, sample = rownames(seqtab), input_reads = track[, "dada2_input"], filtered_reads = track[, "filtered"], merged_reads = track[, "merged"], final_reads = track[, "nonchim"], retention = track[, "final_perc_reads_retained"], n_ASVs = rowSums(seqtab > 0), sample_type = case_when( str_detect(sample, "Extract-ctrl$") ~ "Extraction control", str_detect(sample, "NTC$") ~ "PCR control", TRUE ~ "Biological" ) ) }) ``` ::: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} # 1. Combine DADA2 tracking data ----------------------------------------- qc_tracking <- purrr::map_dfr(markers, function(m) { get(paste0("track_", m)) %>% as.data.frame() %>% tibble::rownames_to_column("sample") %>% mutate( marker = m, sample_type = case_when( str_detect(sample, "Extract-ctrl$") ~ "Extraction control", str_detect(sample, "NTC$") ~ "PCR control", TRUE ~ "Biological" ) ) }) # 2. Calculate median reads at each processing step ----------------------- qc_steps <- qc_tracking %>% filter(sample_type == "Biological") %>% group_by(marker) %>% summarise( across( c(dada2_input, filtered, dada_f, merged, nonchim), median ), .groups = "drop" ) %>% pivot_longer( cols = -marker, names_to = "step", values_to = "median_reads" ) %>% mutate( step = factor( step, levels = c("dada2_input", "filtered", "dada_f", "merged", "nonchim") ) ) # 3. Figure: DADA2 read retention ---------------------------------------- p_retention <- ggplot( qc_steps, aes(x = step, y = median_reads, group = 1) ) + geom_line(colour = "#0072B2", linewidth = 0.8) + geom_point(colour = "#0072B2", size = 2.5) + facet_wrap(~ marker, scales = "free_y") + scale_x_discrete(labels = c( dada2_input = "Input", filtered = "Filtered", dada_f = "Denoised F", merged = "Merged", nonchim = "Nonchim" )) + scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::label_comma()) + labs( x = NULL, y = "Median reads per sample", title = "DADA2 read retention across markers", subtitle = "Biological samples only" ) + theme_bw(base_size = 11) + theme( panel.grid.minor = element_blank(), axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 40, hjust = 1) ) print(p_retention) # 4. Figure: Final sequencing depth per sample ---------------------------- p_depth <- qc_samples %>% mutate( marker = factor(marker, levels = markers), sample_type = factor( sample_type, levels = c("Biological", "Extraction control", "PCR control") ), sample_order = as.integer(str_extract(sample, "^[0-9]+")) ) %>% ggplot(aes( x = sample_order, y = final_reads, fill = sample_type )) + geom_col(width = 0.85) + facet_wrap(~ marker, scales = "free_y") + scale_fill_manual(values = c( "Biological" = "#0072B2", "Extraction control" = "#D55E00", "PCR control" = "#CC79A7" )) + scale_x_continuous(breaks = c(1, 10, 20, 30, 34, 35)) + scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::label_comma()) + labs( x = "Sample number", y = "Non-chimeric reads", fill = NULL, title = "Final sequencing depth per sample" ) + theme_bw(base_size = 11) + theme( panel.grid.minor = element_blank(), legend.position = "bottom" ) print(p_depth) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} "dada2_input"] ) %>% ungroup() # Combined plot p_retention_combined <- ggplot( qc_steps_perc, aes(x = step, y = retention, colour = marker, group = marker) ) + geom_line(linewidth = 1) + geom_point(size = 2.5) + scale_x_discrete(labels = c( dada2_input = "Input", filtered = "Filtered", dada_f = "Denoised F", merged = "Merged", nonchim = "Nonchim" )) + scale_y_continuous( breaks = seq(80, 100, 5), labels = scales::label_percent(scale = 1) ) + coord_cartesian(ylim = c(80, 100)) + scale_colour_brewer(palette = "Dark2") + labs( x = NULL, y = "Reads retained (%)", colour = "Marker", title = "DADA2 read retention across markers" ) + theme_bw(base_size = 12) + theme( panel.grid.minor = element_blank(), legend.position = "right" ) p_retention_combined ``` ::: # Calculate rarefaction curves ------------------------------------------- rarefaction <- purrr::map_dfr(markers, function(m) { seqtab <- get(paste0("seqtab_", m)) # Exclude both negative controls seqtab <- seqtab[ !grepl("Extract-ctrl$|NTC$", rownames(seqtab)), , drop = FALSE ] # Remove zero-depth samples seqtab <- seqtab[rowSums(seqtab) > 0, , drop = FALSE] # Depths covering the full range of each sample max_depth <- max(rowSums(seqtab)) depths <- unique(round(seq(1, max_depth, length.out = 60))) purrr::map_dfr(seq_len(nrow(seqtab)), function(i) { sample_depth <- rowSums(seqtab[i, , drop = FALSE]) d <- unique(c( depths[depths <= sample_depth], sample_depth )) tibble( marker = m, sample = rownames(seqtab)[i], depth = d, richness = vapply( d, function(n) as.numeric( vegan::rarefy(seqtab[i, , drop = FALSE], sample = n) ), numeric(1) ) ) }) }) # Summary curves: # Recalculate on a common depth grid for each marker so that # all biological samples contribute at every plotted depth. rarefaction_summary <- purrr::map_dfr(markers, function(m) { x <- get(paste0("seqtab_", m)) # Exclude negative controls x <- x[!grepl("Extract-ctrl$|NTC$", rownames(x)), , drop = FALSE] # Exclude COI sample 22 if (m == "COI") { x <- x[!grepl("^22_COI_", rownames(x)), , drop = FALSE] } depths <- unique(round(seq(1, min(rowSums(x)), length.out = 60))) purrr::map_dfr(depths, function(d) { richness <- as.numeric(vegan::rarefy(x, sample = d)) tibble( marker = m, depth = d, mean_richness = mean(richness), sd_richness = sd(richness) ) }) }) # Combined figure -------------------------------------------------------- p_rarefaction_combined <- ggplot( rarefaction_summary, aes(x = depth, y = mean_richness, colour = marker, fill = marker) ) + geom_ribbon( aes( ymin = pmax(0, mean_richness - sd_richness), ymax = mean_richness + sd_richness ), alpha = 0.15, colour = NA ) + geom_line(linewidth = 1.1) + scale_colour_brewer(palette = "Dark2") + scale_fill_brewer(palette = "Dark2") + scale_x_continuous(labels = scales::label_comma()) + labs( x = "Sequencing depth (reads)", y = "Expected ASV richness", colour = "Marker", fill = "Marker", title = "Rarefaction curves across markers", subtitle = "Mean ± SD across biological samples" ) + theme_bw(base_size = 12) + theme( panel.grid.minor = element_blank(), legend.position = "right" ) markers <- c("16S", "18S", "COI", "MiFish", "ITS", "rbcL") for (m in markers) { seqtab <- get(paste0("seqtab_", m)) taxa <- get(paste0("taxa_", m)) # Check that taxonomy and ASV sequences match stopifnot(setequal(colnames(seqtab), rownames(taxa))) # Align taxonomy to the ASV table taxa <- taxa[colnames(seqtab), , drop = FALSE] # Assign simple ASV identifiers asv_ids <- paste0("ASV", seq_len(ncol(seqtab))) sequences <- colnames(seqtab) colnames(seqtab) <- asv_ids rownames(taxa) <- asv_ids # Sample metadata metadata <- data.frame( SampleID = rownames(seqtab), SampleType = ifelse( grepl("Extract-ctrl$", rownames(seqtab)), "Extraction control", ifelse( grepl("NTC$", rownames(seqtab)), "PCR control", "Biological" ) ), row.names = rownames(seqtab) ) # Create phyloseq object ps <- phyloseq( otu_table(seqtab, taxa_are_rows = FALSE), tax_table(as.matrix(taxa)), sample_data(metadata), refseq(Biostrings::DNAStringSet( setNames(sequences, asv_ids) )) ) assign(paste0("ps_", m), ps) } # 18S - PR2 colnames(tax_table(ps_18S)) <- c( "Domain", "Supergroup", "Division", "Subdivision", "Class", "Order", "Family", "Genus", "Species" ) # rbcL - Diat.barcode 16.3 colnames(tax_table(ps_rbcL)) <- c( "Empire", "Kingdom", "Subkingdom", "Phylum", "Subphylum", "Class", "Order", "Family", "Genus", "Species" ) ``` ::: ## Proportion of unassigned ASVs ::: {.cell} Keep biological samples only ps <- subset_samples(ps, SampleType == "Biological") ps <- prune_samples(sample_sums(ps) > 0, ps) ps <- prune_taxa(taxa_sums(ps) > 0, ps) # 2. Replace missing class assignments tax <- as(tax_table(ps), "matrix") tax[, "Class"][ is.na(tax[, "Class"]) | trimws(tax[, "Class"]) == "" | tolower(trimws(tax[, "Class"])) %in% c("na", "unclassified") ] <- "Unassigned" tax_table(ps) <- tax_table(tax) # 3. Agglomerate to Class ps_class <- tax_glom( ps, taxrank = "Class", NArm = FALSE ) # 4. Convert to relative abundance ps_rel <- microbiome::transform( ps_class, "compositional" ) # 5. Select top classes by mean relative abundance top_classes <- microbiome::top_taxa( ps_rel, n = top_n ) # 6. Melt and group remaining classes df <- psmelt(ps_rel) %>% mutate( Class = as.character(Class), Class_plot = if_else( OTU %in% top_classes | Class == "Unassigned", Class, "Other" ), Number = as.integer( stringr::str_extract(Sample, "^[0-9]+") ) ) %>% group_by(Sample, Number, Class_plot) %>% summarise( Abundance = sum(Abundance), .groups = "drop" ) # 7. Assign colours plot_colors <- setNames( rep(my_colors, length.out = length(class_order)), class_order ) if ("Unassigned" %in% class_order) { plot_colors["Unassigned"] <- "#666666" } if ("Other" %in% class_order) { plot_colors["Other"] <- "#C0C0C0" } # 9. Plot ggplot( df, aes( x = factor(Number, levels = 1:33), y = Abundance, fill = Class_plot ) ) + geom_col(width = 0.85) + scale_fill_manual( values = plot_colors, drop = FALSE ) + scale_y_continuous( labels = scales::percent, expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0)) ) + labs( title = paste0(marker, " — Class-level composition"), x = "Sample number", y = "Relative abundance (%)", fill = "Class" ) + theme_classic(base_size = 12) + theme( axis.text.x = element_text( angle = 45, hjust = 1 ), legend.position = "bottom", legend.direction = "horizontal" ) + guides( fill = guide_legend(nrow = 5, byrow = TRUE) ) } ``` ::: # Class-level taxonomical composition ## 16S ::: {.cell} ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](Context_files/figure-html/unnamed-chunk-18-1.png){width=1152} ::: ::: ## 18S ::: {.cell} ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](Context_files/figure-html/unnamed-chunk-19-1.png){width=1152} ::: ::: ## COI ::: {.cell} ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](Context_files/figure-html/unnamed-chunk-20-1.png){width=1152} ::: ::: ## MiFish ::: {.cell} ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](Context_files/figure-html/unnamed-chunk-21-1.png){width=1152} ::: ::: ## ITS ::: {.cell} ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](Context_files/figure-html/unnamed-chunk-22-1.png){width=1152} ::: ::: ## rbcL ::: {.cell} ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](Context_files/figure-html/unnamed-chunk-23-1.png){width=1152} ::: :::
